clue.text: Sleazy guy's article in Paris Match on how to open a French letter

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article, 'the'

parts.words: how to open a French letter
parts.note: a letter in French begins 'Cher...', the equivalent of 'Dear...'

explanation.surface: A French magazine runs a piece on letter-writing etiquette, with a smutty undertone about condoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French letter' is British slang for a condom, which steers the reader towards smut; here it is just a letter written in French. 'Match on' only links the two pieces, with Paris Match the French weekly magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecher is a lustful, lewd man, which fits a sleazy fellow exactly.

clue.text: Ex-PM losing head in retreat

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the politician's name is dropped

parts.note: Tony Blair is a former UK prime minister

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is ousted and withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' reads as a verb but is a noun, a hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den, a place to hide away.

clue.text: Millions invested in business stake — it may promote growth

indicators.note: invested in says the abbreviation is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: CO is short for company
a post is a stake driven into the ground
M stands for million

explanation.surface: Millions are put into a business share to help it grow.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial surface hides garden manure.
explanation.definitionFit: Compost is decayed organic matter spread to enrich soil and help plants grow.

clue.text: Old newspaperman, having admitted wrong, made a racket?

indicators.note: having admitted means letting something inside, so the legal wrong goes in

parts.note: ex means former
ED is short for editor
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A former journalist confesses to an error and caused a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a racket' sounds like making noise; a racket is also a criminal extortion scheme, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a protection racket involves extorting money by threats.

clue.text: He preserves 1/6th of an inch marble bust

parts.note: in printing an em, or pica em, measures twelve points, about a sixth of an inch

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of the word marble are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A marble bust is described in strangely precise measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as a sculpture to go with marble, but it is the anagram signal; the em is a printer's unit solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: An embalmer treats corpses with preservatives to stop them decaying.

clue.text: Wrongdoing from the anti-feminist league?

parts.note: a male party is the side opposed to feminists, read playfully
a faction is a group or league within a body

explanation.surface: A men's-rights group is accused of misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as two words suggests a men-only party, hence 'anti-feminist league?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Malefaction is evildoing or crime.

clue.text: Regularly wearied by a politician's current measure

indicators.note: by says the picked letters sit beside the other pieces

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A politician is worn out at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'wearied', giving ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the SI unit of electric current.

clue.text: Objectively, I gain ground introducing new import

parts.note: the objective case of I is me

indicators.note: introducing says the abbreviation for new is brought into the reworked letters
ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of the word gain are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone gains land by bringing in foreign goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'import' looks like trade goods but means significance; GAIN rearranged as ANIG takes N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The import of a remark is its sense or significance.

clue.text: Recorder playing air gets in right runs

indicators.note: in says the reworked letters sit between the two single letters

parts.note: R stands for runs in cricket scoring

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played around with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A recorder player gets the tune right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' looks like the musical instrument, encouraged by 'playing air'; it is an official who records births and deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is an official keeping records such as births, marriages and deaths.

clue.text: Hot drink and porridge for him!

parts.note: hot in the sense of fashionable or popular, as in the in thing
maté is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: A hot drink and a bowl of porridge make a man's breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang porridge means a prison sentence, from the oats once served in jails; the definition says the answer is someone doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a sentence is doing porridge, so porridge is what a convict's life consists of.

clue.text: Force to apprehend associates returning directly

indicators.note: returning means the whole string of pieces is read from end to start

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravitational force in physics
to nab is to arrest or catch
pals are friends or associates

explanation.surface: Police are sent to arrest a criminal's associates as they come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the whole string, not just one piece; 'Force' looks like a verb but is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-bang is an informal adverb meaning directly or exactly, as in slap-bang in the middle.

clue.text: Prepared for roistering around area where buffets are common

indicators.note: around says the reworked letters go round the abbreviation for area
prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Revellers get ready for a rowdy night in a place where buffets are always on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffets' suggests food spread out on tables; it means blows from the wind. 'Prepared' signals the anagram and 'around' puts the area letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roaring Forties are the stormy latitudes of the Southern Ocean, where strong westerly winds batter ships constantly.

clue.text: Personality disorder raging in Tom Cruise

indicators.note: raging means wild and out of control, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star is said to have a psychological problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuroticism is a personality trait marked by anxiety and emotional instability.

clue.text: Abandoned UK province rejected Luther's Reformed Church

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the abbreviation for the province is reversed

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is sometimes called the Province of the UK

indicators.note: reformed means re-formed or reshaped, so the letters of Luther are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A Protestant church in Northern Ireland turns its back on the Lutheran tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' looks like a nod to the Reformation and Luther, but it signals the anagram of LUTHER into THELUR; 'rejected' turns NI into IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being left in the lurch is the idiom for being deserted in a moment of difficulty.

clue.text: Mail late as express isn't complete — that's awkward

indicators.note: isn't complete means only a part of these words is used, with letters missing at each end

explanation.surface: Express post arriving late is a bit embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop MA from 'Mail' and XPRESS from 'express' to leave the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill at ease means uncomfortable or awkward.

clue.text: Foreign ruler with recipe for jelly

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman military commander or chief officer
R, from Latin recipe 'take', heads prescriptions

explanation.surface: A ruler from abroad shares a recipe for jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is the gelatinous substance from seaweed used to set foods and grow cultures.

clue.text: House is grand; nothing dirty's shown up

indicators.note: shown up in a down clue means the run of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
nil means nothing
lewd means dirty or smutty; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A grand house turns out to be filthy after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' only links; 'shown up' reverses the whole string so it reads upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a house or home.

clue.text: Desire endless hot soak

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the synonym for desire is cut off

parts.note: lust is strong desire
H stands for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a long hot bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' reads as a verb about baths, but it is a noun for a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a lush and a soak are informal terms for a habitual drunkard.

clue.text: Tongue was strained greeting a couple from Lithuania

indicators.note: strained means twisted out of shape, so the letters of was are rearranged

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: a couple from means the first two letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: Someone strains to say hello in Lithuanian.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu language widely spoken in East Africa.

clue.text: Disgruntled peasant gets stuck in to more agreeable beverage

indicators.note: gets stuck in says the rebel's name is pushed inside the other pieces

parts.note: nicer means more pleasant or agreeable
Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381

explanation.surface: An angry farm labourer muscles in on a nicer drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led England's Peasants' Revolt of 1381, hence the disgruntled peasant; 'gets stuck in' puts him inside the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a carbonated soft drink flavoured with quinine, often mixed with gin.

clue.text: He has left the property

indicators.note: has left means the pronoun is removed from the following phrase

parts.note: an estate is land or property

explanation.surface: A man has bequeathed his estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HE from THE ESTATE; read whole, the clue describes someone who died leaving a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testate person is one who died having made a valid will disposing of their goods.

clue.text: German combatant in the Battle of the Bulge?

definitions.text: combatant in the Battle of the Bulge?
definitions.meaning: someone fighting their waistline, a slimmer

explanation.definitionFit: Dieter is a German forename, and someone dieting battles bodily bulges.

clue.text: Conservative attitude is fixed aim in old artist

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traditional painter sticks firmly to one goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' only links; 'fixed' reads as steadfast but signals rearranging AIM IN OLD ARTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditionalism is adherence to established customs and resistance to change, a conservative outlook.

clue.text: Footballing whiz dropping back in muddle

indicators.note: dropping back means the last letter of the footballer's name is lost

parts.note: Lionel Messi is an Argentine football star

explanation.surface: A football star drops back into a confused defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a muddle or confused state.

clue.text: High-flying female gulls heard by a Roman road

indicators.note: by says the next piece sits beside the one before it

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

indicators.note: heard says the word for gulls is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: to gull someone is to trick them, so gulls means tricks

explanation.surface: Seabirds are heard calling beside an old Roman road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gulls' looks like the birds, which suits 'High-flying', but it is the verb for deceiving.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviatrix is a dated word for a woman pilot.

clue.text: Silver, say, is good value

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good
to rate something is to value it

explanation.surface: Silver is worth a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver is Long John Silver, the pirate in Treasure Island, not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is a pirate, hence an example signalled by 'say'.

clue.text: Online swine strikes with pointed remarks

parts.note: E as a prefix stands for electronic, as in email
a pig is a swine
rams means strikes forcefully

explanation.surface: An internet troll lashes out with cutting comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigrams are short, witty sayings with a sharp point.

clue.text: Going out with Frenchman from the right society

indicators.note: from the right means the name is read leftwards, backwards

parts.note: Serge is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: Leaving with a Frenchman from a right-wing club.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is the act of exiting, a formal word for leaving.
